question: What minimum geometry and operational restrictions apply to a bicycle box, and how must optional green pavement be applied?
model_answer: Direct Answer: A bicycle box must be at least 10 feet deep, measured from its upstream edge (nearest the motor vehicle stop line) to its downstream edge (nearest the crosswalk or intersection), and must contain at least one bicycle symbol marking. Green-colored pavement is optional, but if it is used it must cover the full limits of the bicycle box, and bicycle boxes are one of the only permitted applications of green-colored pavement. The evidence provided does not describe additional operational restrictions (such as turn or signal-phase restrictions) for bicycle boxes. Standards (mandatory): - "If used, the distance from the upstream edge of the bicycle box that is nearest to the stop line for motor vehicles to the downstream edge of the bicycle box that is nearest the crosswalk or intersection shall be at least 10 feet. At least one bicycle symbol marking (see Figure 9E-12) shall be used in the bicycle box." - "If used, green-colored pavement shall be used in the full limits of the bicycle box." - "If used, green-colored pavement shall be limited to: A. Bicycle lanes..., B. Extensions of bicycle lanes through intersections..., C. Extensions of bicycle lanes through areas where motor vehicles enter a mandatory turn lane in which motor vehicles must weave across bicyclists in bicycle lanes..., D. Two-stage bicycle turn boxes..., E. Bicycle Boxes..., and F. As a background for bicycle detector symbols...." Guidance (recommended): - If green-colored pavement is used within separated bicycle lanes on an independent alignment, it should be used only at the entrances to those facilities from roadways open to public travel or at conflict, weaving, or crossing locations. Options (permitted): - Green-colored pavement may be installed for the entire length of a bicycle lane or bicycle lane extension, or for only a portion (or portions) of it. (Note: this option addresses bicycle lanes/extensions; for bicycle boxes, the full-limits Standard governs.) Citations: - Section 9E.12 Standard §6 (p.1105) - Section 9E.12 Standard §13 (p.1106) - Section 3H.06 Standard §2 (p.626) - Section 3H.06 Guidance §5 (p.626) - Section 3H.06 Option §7 (p.626) - Section 3H.06 Support §1 (p.625)
gold_answer: The box must be at least 10 feet from its upstream edge near the motor-vehicle stop line to its downstream edge near the crosswalk or intersection, must include at least one bicycle symbol, and turns on red must be prohibited from the lane containing the box. If green pavement is used, it must fill the full limits of the bicycle box.
